name: WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology
specimen: Sputum, bronchial washings/brushings, BAL, EBUS/EUS-FNA, transthoracic FNAB
use: All respiratory cytology specimens: exfoliative (sputum, washings, brushings, BAL) and FNAB (EBUS-TBNA, transbronchial, transthoracic).
not_use: Mediastinal lymph nodes may be reported by lymph node system when the question is nodal (staging).

adequacy.title: Adequacy
items: No numerical threshold; assess relative to clinical/imaging target.
Sputum: alveolar macrophages indicate deep sample.
EBUS lymph node: lymphocyte-rich material (some use ≥40 lymphocytes/HPF in cellular areas) or diagnostic lesional cells.
ROSE recommended; triage for cell block and molecular testing.

categories.name: Insufficient / Inadequate / Non-diagnostic
categories.definition: Material insufficient or non-representative for diagnosis, given clinical/imaging context.

rom.source: WHO Reporting System (IAC-IARC), 1st ed – book chapter text
WHO Reporting System (IAC-IARC), 1st ed – book chapter text – by specimen

categories.management: Clinical-radiological correlation; repeat sampling (EBUS/CT-guided FNAB with ROSE) or core/surgical biopsy.
criteria: Acellular or scant, poorly preserved, obscured material.
Only normal bronchial cells/alveolar macrophages from a discrete mass (non-representative).
Sputum without alveolar macrophages (not deep cough sample).

diagnoses.name: Scant non-representative material
diagnoses.final: Insufficient/Inadequate/Non-diagnostic (WHO Lung System). Scant non-representative material.
diagnoses.comment: Material is insufficient/not representative of the radiological lesion. Repeat sampling recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: WHO Lung System – Insufficient/Inadequate/Non-diagnostic

diagnoses.name: Sputum without alveolar macrophages
diagnoses.final: Insufficient/Inadequate/Non-diagnostic (WHO Lung System). Sputum without alveolar macrophages.
diagnoses.comment: Sample is salivary; not representative of lower respiratory tract. Repeat early-morning deep-cough sputum (×3).
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: WHO Lung System – Insufficient/Inadequate/Non-diagnostic

categories.name: Benign
categories.definition: Specific benign diagnosis or benign findings concordant with clinical-imaging context.

rom.source: WHO Reporting System (IAC-IARC), 1st ed – book chapter text – general
WHO Reporting System (IAC-IARC), 1st ed – book chapter text – by specimen

categories.management: Clinical-radiological correlation; if discordant, repeat sampling/biopsy.
criteria: Granulomatous inflammation, infections, abscess, benign neoplasms (hamartoma), reactive changes, organising pneumonia patterns when concordant.

diagnoses.name: Granulomatous inflammation (necrotising/non-necrotising)
diagnoses.final: Benign (WHO Lung System). Granulomatous inflammation (necrotising/non-necrotising).
diagnoses.comment: Stains for AFB/fungi and CBNAAT/culture recommended; sarcoidosis vs tuberculosis per clinical context.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: WHO Lung System – Benign

diagnoses.name: Tuberculosis (AFB positive)
diagnoses.final: Benign (WHO Lung System). Tuberculosis (AFB positive).
diagnoses.comment: Mycobacterial infection confirmed by ZN stain/CBNAAT.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: WHO Lung System – Benign

diagnoses.final: Benign (WHO Lung System). Fungal infection (Aspergillus, Cryptococcus, Histoplasma, Mucor, Pneumocystis).
diagnoses.comment: Specify organism; GMS/PAS; culture.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: WHO Lung System – Benign

diagnoses.name: Acute inflammation / abscess
diagnoses.final: Benign (WHO Lung System). Acute inflammation / abscess.

diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: WHO Lung System – Benign

diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: WHO Lung System – Benign

diagnoses.final: Benign (WHO Lung System). Benign lymph node (EBUS) / sarcoidosis.

diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: WHO Lung System – Benign

categories.name: Atypical
categories.definition: Mostly benign features with some atypia, insufficient for suspicious/malignant.

rom.source: WHO Reporting System (IAC-IARC), 1st ed – book chapter text – by specimen
WHO Reporting System (IAC-IARC), 1st ed – book chapter text

categories.management: Repeat sampling with ancillary tests, or biopsy; MDT discussion.
criteria: Reactive vs neoplastic atypia (e.g. type II pneumocyte hyperplasia, squamous metaplasia, therapy effect).
Low cellularity atypical cells; mucinous/lepidic-type cells with minimal atypia.

diagnoses.name: Atypical epithelial cells
diagnoses.final: Atypical (WHO Lung System). Atypical epithelial cells.
diagnoses.comment: Reactive atypia vs neoplasm; repeat sampling/biopsy recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: WHO Lung System – Atypical

diagnoses.name: Atypical squamous cells
diagnoses.final: Atypical (WHO Lung System). Atypical squamous cells.
diagnoses.comment: Squamous metaplasia/reactive vs SCC; repeat sampling.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: WHO Lung System – Atypical

diagnoses.name: Atypical lymphoid cells
diagnoses.final: Atypical (WHO Lung System). Atypical lymphoid cells.
diagnoses.comment: Flow cytometry on repeat sample recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: WHO Lung System – Atypical

categories.name: Suspicious for malignancy
categories.definition: Features suggestive of malignancy, insufficient quality/quantity for definitive diagnosis.

rom.source: WHO Reporting System (IAC-IARC), 1st ed – book chapter text

categories.management: Repeat sampling/biopsy with ancillary studies; treatment after confirmation.
criteria: Few highly atypical cells; obscured/degenerated malignant-appearing cells.
Suspicious for specific tumour (adenocarcinoma, SCC, small cell, carcinoid).

diagnoses.name: Suspicious for adenocarcinoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious for malignancy (WHO Lung System). Suspicious for adenocarcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Repeat sampling with cell block for IHC/biomarkers.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: WHO Lung System – Suspicious for malignancy

diagnoses.name: Suspicious for squamous cell carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious for malignancy (WHO Lung System). Suspicious for squamous cell carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Repeat sampling/biopsy.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: WHO Lung System – Suspicious for malignancy

diagnoses.name: Suspicious for small cell carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious for malignancy (WHO Lung System). Suspicious for small cell carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Confirm with IHC on repeat sample.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: WHO Lung System – Suspicious for malignancy

diagnoses.name: Suspicious for malignancy, NOS
diagnoses.final: Suspicious for malignancy (WHO Lung System). Suspicious for malignancy, NOS.
diagnoses.comment: Clinical, radiological and MDT correlation recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: WHO Lung System – Suspicious for malignancy

categories.name: Malignant
categories.definition: Unequivocal malignancy; specify type using WHO thoracic classification; use NSCLC-NOS / favour with IHC when morphology unclear.

rom.source: WHO Reporting System (IAC-IARC), 1st ed – book chapter text

categories.management: Treat per oncology; ensure material for predictive biomarkers (EGFR, ALK, ROS1, KRAS, BRAF, MET, RET, NTRK, PD-L1).
criteria: Adenocarcinoma: 3-D clusters, vacuolated cytoplasm, nucleoli; TTF1/Napsin A+.
NSCLC, favour adenocarcinoma/SCC per IHC; NSCLC-NOS if IHC null.
Small cell carcinoma: moulding, salt-and-pepper chromatin, crush; INSM1/synaptophysin+.
Carcinoid (typical/atypical), LCNEC, metastases, lymphoma, mesothelioma (pleural), sarcoma.

diagnoses.name: Adenocarcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (WHO Lung System). Adenocarcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Predictive biomarker testing recommended on cell block (EGFR, ALK, ROS1, PD-L1 etc.).
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: WHO Lung System – Malignant
